extends.new-data: Year 5 reports Solarize reached 5.4 MW installed, expanded statewide, and generated updated savings and installation metrics.
Voters authorized the SEU in November 2024, launch work began immediately, a waitlist was created, and $5 million was secured for startup.
The source adds DTE fuel-mix context, describes the new heating franchise and climate agreement with the city, and notes continued MPSC gas-case interventions.
Year 5 adds a DOE-backed Bryant neighborhood networked geothermal project, a citywide geothermal feasibility study with Stantec, and Catherine Street/Bryant installations.
The source adds sustainability and geothermal integration details for affordable housing projects at Catherine Street and support for Stimson Apartments.
Ann Arbor's Home Energy Rebates launched with over 650 claimed rebates covering weatherization, appliances, batteries, electrical upgrades, and e-bikes.
Year 5 adds the A2ZERO Heat Pump Concierge, contractor education, and broader residential electrification support infrastructure.
The city reports over 40% EV adoption in the light-duty fleet and nearly 30% electrification across the total city fleet.
The source adds a commercial EV charger giveaway program and a $2.8 million federal grant to expand public charging.
Year 5 reports two additional electric refuse trucks purchased, four total on order, and grant support from the American Lung Association.
OSI supported TheRide's successful $25 million federal grant application for zero-emission buses and refueling stations.
The city brought the Green Rental Housing ordinance forward for council consideration as a minimum health, comfort, and efficiency standard.
Benchmarking implementation continued with buildings over 20,000 square feet working toward compliance through collaboration with the 2030 District.
OSI funded county service expansion and secured Bryant-focused MPSC funding for weatherization, electrification, and decarbonization upgrades.
The A2ZERO Green Business Challenge expanded with Fresh Coast Climate Solutions support, interns, and plans to scale to 50 businesses.
Strategy 4 work in year 5 centered heavily on supporting the draft Comprehensive Land Use Plan with sustainability as a core pillar.
The source adds bike lane, bike parking, crosswalk, lighting, cargo-bike, and dashboard progress updates plus new walk/bike recognitions.
Year 5 highlights the Local Food Fest, a draft Sustainable Food Framework, and continued local food-system engagement.
VegMichigan collaboration reached over 1,700 residents and more than 400 first-time participants through the Plant-Based Pledge.
The source adds grant-funded action-plan development, resident advisory engagement, business-planning RFPs, and year 6 priority to co-design the strategy.
Public Works received support for staffing expansion while developing broader commercial recycling and compost service strategies.
The source notes Public Works is developing a strategy to expand compost services citywide.
OSI received EPA funding for a small food retailer refrigerant management program targeting at least 75 businesses and major emissions reductions.
Ann Arbor surpassed 10,000 trees planted, distributed over 11,000 total trees, and won a $1 million American Forests grant for tree equity work.
Year 5 adds cohort growth to 118 trained ambassadors, recruitment events, a StoryMap, and an annual Ambassador Summit.
The source adds preparedness seminars, emergency-kit distributions, ward-party outreach, and plans to scale household preparedness programming.
Eight additional air-quality monitors were installed, bringing the network total to ten with live dashboard data.
Year 5 adds Green Baxter Court solar-plus-storage procurement, Peace Neighborhood Center upgrades, and resilience-network coordination work.
The report shows continued millage-like implementation capacity through rebates, neighborhood decarbonization support, and broad cross-strategy program delivery.
The source notes a Sustaining Ann Arbor Together grant award to SunBundle.

theme-connections: Source ties SEU authorization, utility advocacy, and geothermal deployment into a broader local energy-system transition.
Year 5 shows rebates and grant funding acting as cross-strategy implementation engines across buildings, mobility, and resilience.
Bryant neighborhood emerges as a multi-strategy decarbonization district linking affordability, geothermal, weatherization, and engagement.
Resilience work increasingly overlaps with energy infrastructure through solar-plus-storage, nanogrids, air monitoring, and preparedness.
Food systems and circular economy efforts are becoming more formalized through frameworks, coalitions, and measurable diversion programs.
